filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-01.question: In Philippians 2:3, Paul told each one to consider himself superior to all others.
filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-01.feedbackCorrect: It is the opposite: consider others superior to yourself.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Philippians 2:3: humility looks toward the other.

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-01.hint: See the direction of considering in the verse.

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-02.question: In Philippians 2:8, tap how far Christ's obedience went.
filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-02.learningObjective: Identify the limit of Christ's obedience.
filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-02.feedbackCorrect: His obedience did not stop short of the hardest end.

feedbackWrong.a: Man is the form he took, not the limit of obedience.
feedbackWrong.c: That specifies the kind of death, after the limit named.

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-02.hint: Look for the word right after "até à".

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-03.question: According to Philippians 2:8, how did Christ humble himself?
filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-03.feedbackCorrect: His descent goes as far as obedience on the cross.

feedbackWrong.a: He took on suffering; he did not refuse it.
feedbackWrong.b: He did not flee: he gave himself in obedience.
feedbackWrong.c: The cross exposed, not hid, his mission.

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-03.hint: See the end of the downward path.

options.b: Fleeing from people who rejected him
options.c: Hiding who he was until old age
options.d: Becoming obedient unto death on a cross

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-04.question: Put Philippians 2:7 in the order of the text.
filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-04.learningObjective: Recognize the sequence of Christ's descent.
filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-04.feedbackCorrect: He empties himself, becomes a servant, and is made like men.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with his emptying of himself.

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-04.hint: The order begins with him emptying himself.

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-05.question: In Philippians 2:7, what form did Christ take when he emptied himself?
filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-05.feedbackCorrect: The one who was God takes the place of one who serves.

feedbackWrong.a: Judgment is not the form he takes when he descends.
feedbackWrong.b: He will be recognized as King, but here he takes another place.

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-05.hint: It is the place of one who serves others.

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-06.question: What does Philippians 2:5 communicate that connects to this context?
filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-06.learningObjective: Link the church's life to the mind of Christ.
filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-06.feedbackCorrect: The remedy for rivalry is to have the mind of Christ.

feedbackWrong.a: Christ drew near and served; he did not keep distance.
feedbackWrong.c: Rivalry and vanity are the problem, not the remedy.

filipenses-sem-fp-02-humildade-06.hint: See whose mind is asked for.

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-01.question: In Philippians 2:9, God exalted Christ because he humbled himself unto death on a cross.
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-01.learningObjective: Understand the link between humiliation and exaltation.
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-01.feedbackCorrect: "Por isso" links the exaltation to his obedient humiliation.

feedbackWrong.false: The verse begins by linking exaltation to his descent.

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-01.hint: See the first two words of the verse.

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-02.question: In Philippians 2:3, tap the little word that turns rivalry's order into humility.
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-02.feedbackCorrect: Nothing from rivalry; with humility, says the turn.

feedbackWrong.b: That opens the prohibition; it does not make the turn.
feedbackWrong.c: That is one of the evils forbidden, not the turn.

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-02.hint: Look for the short conjunction before "humildade".

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-03.question: How does Christ's path in Philippians 2:6–8 answer the rivalry of 2:3?
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-03.learningObjective: Relate Christ's example to the church's life.
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-03.feedbackCorrect: The opposite of rivalry: letting go and serving unto the cross.

feedbackWrong.b: He does not fight for superiority: he descends to servant.
feedbackWrong.c: The one who serves here is he, not those around him.
feedbackWrong.d: He was made like men; he did not withdraw from them.

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-03.hint: Compare clinging to rights with emptying oneself.

options.a: Instead of clinging to his right, he made himself a servant
options.b: He defeated rivals by showing he was superior to all
options.c: He demanded that everyone serve him first on earth
options.d: He left people behind to live alone in heaven

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-04.question: How does Christ's descent chain together in Philippians 2:6–8?
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-04.learningObjective: Understand the stages of Christ's descent.
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-04.feedbackCorrect: Not clinging, emptying himself, and obeying unto the cross.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with what he did not insist on holding.

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-04.hint: The cross is the lowest point of the descent.

options.a: He does not cling to being equal with God
options.b: He empties himself and takes the form of a servant
options.c: He obeys unto death on a cross

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-05.question: In Philippians 2:5, what must the church have in itself, as was in Christ?
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-05.learningObjective: Understand what the church must imitate in Christ.
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-05.feedbackCorrect: It is not only to admire: it is to have the same way of feeling.

feedbackWrong.a: Debating from rivalry is precisely the problem.
feedbackWrong.b: Fear is not what Paul tells them to copy from Christ.

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-05.hint: It is Christ's inward way toward others.

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-06.question: What links Philippians 2:7 to Mark 10:45?
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-06.learningObjective: Relate the form of a servant to Jesus' words.
filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-06.feedbackCorrect: Jesus himself said: he came not to be served, but to serve.

feedbackWrong.a: He serves even to giving his life; he flees from nothing.
feedbackWrong.b: Both texts invert greatness by domination.

filipenses-cam-fp-02-humildade-06.hint: See what the Son of Man came for.

options.a: A servant who flees from suffering
options.c: The Son of Man came to serve

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-01.question: Philippians 2:6–7 teaches that Jesus stopped being God when he took the form of a servant.
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-01.learningObjective: Interpret the descent without erasing who Christ is.
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-01.feedbackCorrect: He existed in the form of God and takes that of a servant: addition, not swap.

feedbackWrong.true: The hymn keeps both forms over the same Christ.

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-01.hint: See what he already was before descending.

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-02.question: In Philippians 2:6, tap what Christ already existed as, before emptying himself.
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-02.learningObjective: Ground in the text who Christ was before the descent.
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-02.feedbackCorrect: The descent starts from above: he already existed as God.

feedbackWrong.b: That speaks of the equality he did not use for himself.
feedbackWrong.c: That is what he did not consider doing, not what he was.

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-02.hint: Look for the first description of him in the verse.

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-03.question: What reading do Philippians 2:6–9 support about humility and exaltation?
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the hymn supports.
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-03.feedbackCorrect: The descent to servant ends in exaltation given by the Father.

feedbackWrong.b: The hymn begins by affirming that he existed as God.
feedbackWrong.d: Humility here is serving the other, not hating yourself.

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-03.hint: Link "por isso" to the prior descent.

options.a: Whoever humbles himself as a servant is exalted by God
options.b: Christ is only a moral example, without being God
options.c: Exaltation is a prize of luck for a few
options.d: Humility is thinking that you are worth nothing

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-04.question: What sequence reveals the sense of Philippians 2:6–11?
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-04.learningObjective: See the full arc of the hymn of Christ.
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-04.feedbackCorrect: From God to servant, from servant to Lord confessed by all.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with who he was before descending.

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-04.hint: The universal confession closes the hymn.

options.a: The Son exists in the form of God
options.b: He descends to an obedient servant unto the cross
options.c: Every tongue confesses him as Lord

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-05.question: In Philippians 2:9, what did God grant Christ above all others?
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-05.learningObjective: Remember the center of Christ's exaltation.
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-05.feedbackCorrect: At his name every knee will bow, says the hymn.

feedbackWrong.a: Throne is not the hymn's word in this sentence.
feedbackWrong.b: No temple is granted in this exaltation.

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-05.hint: It is before him that every knee bows.

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-06.question: What links Philippians 2:7 to John 1:14?
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-06.learningObjective: Link Christ's descent to the incarnation in John.
filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-06.feedbackCorrect: John says the same mystery: the divine Word became flesh.

feedbackWrong.a: Flesh is taken on in love, not as a prison.
feedbackWrong.b: He remains God when he becomes flesh, in both texts.

filipenses-pro-fp-02-humildade-06.hint: See what the Word became in John.

options.a: Flesh as a prison of the spirit

estudo:fp-02-humildade.context: Paul wants a united church, without rivalry or vanity. For that, he does not give only an order: he shows the path of Christ himself, who descended from God to servant and to the cross.
estudo:fp-02-humildade.focusQuestion: In what relationship do you need to stop defending yourself and start serving?
estudo:fp-02-humildade.keywordGloss: The mind of Christ: instead of clinging to what is his, he empties himself and serves to the end.
facts: Paul asks the church to share the same mind and be united in soul.
With humility, each one must consider others superior to himself.
Each one must also care for what is others', not only his own.
Christ, existing in the form of God, did not cling to being equal with God.
He emptied himself, taking the form of a servant.
He humbled himself, obedient unto death, even death on a cross.
